vision.title: The Adventure Begins
vision.premise: Keen leaves home for Crystal Cove wearing borrowed confidence and his father’s empty wristbands; a storm strips away the performance until he must choose real courage to save Squeaky and arrive not as a boy who “has this,” but as a bear who knows he is held by family, memory, and the new circle waiting for him.
vision.dramaticQuestion: When Keen’s brave face is taken apart by distance, weather, and someone else’s need, can he stop pretending he is fearless and let true courage carry him through?
vision.theme: Courage is not being alone without fear; courage is feeling the fear, feeling who loves you, and acting anyway.
vision.externalJourney: Keen departs the pier, meets Squeaky, gets caught in a storm, loses his map and boat, follows Squeaky into rough water, frees her from the drift net, is rescued by her, and reaches Crystal Cove where the bears welcome him and his aquamarine crystal settles into his father’s wristbands.
vision.internalJourney: Keen begins by performing certainty for his Mum and for himself: “I’ve got this, Mum.” The water reveals that confidence as borrowed. He becomes lost, afraid, and then faced with Squeaky’s need. His turn is not a power-up; it is surrender into sincerity. The wristbands glow when his father’s love, his Mum’s promise, and Keen’s own choice align. By the end, “Hi… I’m Keen” lands as a real introduction, not a brave mask.
vision.relationshipChanges: The heart relationship is Keen and his Mum: she lets him go without letting the ache become a cage, and he carries her love into the unknown. Aida becomes the bridge between home and Cove, witnessing what Mum cannot see and sending reassurance back. Keen and Squeaky begin as playful strangers and become rescue partners. Fuzzby and Zenny carry the comic relationship spine: his frantic self-importance needs her clean truth, and her restraint lets his big feeling stay lovable rather than noisy. The bears move from distant witnesses to chosen family.
vision.emotionalCurve: The episode opens in play: pollen, bravado, dry affection. It quietly deepens through Aida’s bowl and Mum’s held pride. The goodbye is the first ache, warmed by Keen’s wobble. The open water begins as adventure, then tightens into lostness. The shore scenes widen the fear into communal concern. The nadir is underwater: Keen’s strength fading, Squeaky trapped, the wristbands beginning to glow. The climax releases into action and terror together, then relief arrives wet, breathless, and laughing. The ending warms into belonging but keeps the trace of cost through Mum’s absence and the wristbands’ meaning.
vision.comedyCurve: Comedy starts high and behavioural with Fuzzby converting every failure into proof of mastery, while Zenny’s flat precision punctures him without cruelty. It returns as emergency comedy when Fuzzby is too panicked to be useful until Zenny supplies the truth. After the rescue, comedy becomes release: Keen laughs out terror with “Best… ride… ever!”, Fuzzby instantly mythologizes him, and the honey question turns welcome into friendship appetite. The final laugh is not random; it proves Fuzzby has accepted Keen fully and excessively, exactly as himself.
vision.setupPayoffMap: Fuzzby’s “Nailed it” and “Buzz Crash!!” set up the episode’s false-bravado language, paid off by Keen’s “Still got it!” as the same cover over a much deeper goodbye. The pollen moustache/goatee escalates Fuzzby’s need to look official, paid off when real emergency makes him emotionally sincere but verbally jammed. Aida’s rose-quartz bowl vision sets her as witness-from-a-distance, paid off when she sees Keen in the storm and sends Squeaky home with news for Mum. Mum’s vacant wristbands are planted as grief and protection, paid off underwater when they glow from within and become the vessel for Keen’s aquamarine crystal. Squeaky’s playful arrival at the pier sets trust, paid off when Keen follows her into rough water and later when she saves him. The map gag — “one of the directions” — plants that Keen’s confidence depends on appearing oriented, paid off when the storm takes the map and forces inner orientation. The shore beacon sets communal love across distance, paid off by Keen riding toward the glowing shore.
vision.visualMotifs: Empty wristbands becoming meaningful light. Water as the distance between being protected and choosing for yourself. The boat shrinking against open water. Pollen bravado versus storm truth. Circles: Aida’s bowl, the bears’ gathering circle, the warm circle around Keen on the sand. Light crossing weather: rose-quartz signal, combined beacon, aquamarine settling into family memory. Held paws: Mum placing the wristbands, Keen gripping the net, the group enclosing him without crowding him.
vision.sonicMotifs: Fuzzby’s busy chant and crash rhythm establish comic motion before the storm interrupts it. The crystal bowl note gives way to distant wind, linking Aida’s knowing to the weather coming. Thunder cuts through comedy as the tonal turn. Keen’s repeated “I’ve got this…” shifts from performance to self-steadying. The bears’ joined Crystal Call becomes a signal across fear rather than a solution. The aquamarine note should resolve only after Keen has already acted with sincerity. Squeaky’s chatter begins playful and becomes relational — not language, but trust.
vision.climax: Underwater, Keen reaches Squeaky, the net resists, the current shoves them, and his performed confidence finally has no audience left. The father’s wristbands glow from within; on shore, Aida names the truth: “He’s not alone.” Keen braces, pulls through the glow, tears the net free, and is thrown away by the wave. The rescue completes not because he becomes fearless, but because he acted while afraid — and Squeaky then catches him in return.
vision.resolution: Keen arrives in the shallows, releases the terror as laughter, and meets the Crystal Bears from a place of earned openness. Aida names the courage he has already lived; the aquamarine light appears, splits, and settles into the wristbands, turning inherited love into Keen’s own crystal strength. The final beach walk lets relief breathe through Fuzzby’s honey-friendship obsession, ending with laughter and belonging rather than a lecture.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, proud, and a little tender: the child should feel the thrill of a storm ride and a new friendship; the adult should feel the ache of a parent letting go and the comfort of love that travels farther than the dock. The ending should not feel like the fear vanished — it should feel like Keen now knows what to do with it.

scene.location: Keen’s home pier and the small boat pulling away from the dock
scene.time: Warm golden morning, just before departure
scene.purpose: Turn the adventure from idea into irreversible leaving: Keen performs confidence, Mum gives him his father’s vacant wristbands, and the first small wobble proves the bravery is not yet real but is beginning to be loved into place.
scene.dramaticQuestion: Can Keen leave home without hiding how much leaving costs him and his Mum?
scene.emotionalOwner: Keen, with Keen's Mum carrying the quieter adult ache underneath him.
scene.characterObjectives: Keen wants to prove he is ready and keep the goodbye light enough to survive it. Keen's Mum wants to bless him, protect him through memory, and let him go without turning her fear into a cage. Squeaky wants playful contact and curiosity once the boat leaves.
scene.opposition: The packed boat, the open water, the weight of the wristbands, and the fact that both Keen and his Mum are trying not to make the goodbye too hard.
scene.subtext: Keen’s words say he is ready; his body is still checking whether Mum believes it. Mum’s hands say what her voice nearly cannot: your father is gone, but his love and mine travel with you.
scene.emotionalEntry: Buoyant preparation masking the first pinch of separation.
scene.emotionalExit: Keen is away from the dock, nervous and excited together, with Mum’s promise now physically on him and Squeaky turning departure into relationship.
scene.storyTurn: The wristbands move from Mum’s keeping into Keen’s paws; the journey becomes inheritance, not just adventure.
scene.visualIdentity: Warm pier lines, rope movement in the breeze, the boat as a small floating threshold, and vacant wristbands as the scene’s emotional object.
scene.lightingAtmosphere: Soft golden morning with gentle water reflection; warmth remains, but the open water beyond the pier is cooler and wider.
scene.energyShape: Starts busy and tidy with packing, narrows into a tender handoff, releases into a comic wobble, then opens into gliding adventure with Squeaky.
scene.connectionFromPreviousScene: After the earlier comedy and the growing sense of storm elsewhere, this scene grounds the episode in Keen’s home relationship and makes the cost of leaving specific.
scene.handoverToNextScene: Keen leaves the pier carrying borrowed confidence, family love, and vacant wristbands; the boat’s increasing distance hands the story to open water and the test ahead.
scene.showrunnerNotes: Do not over-sentimentalize the goodbye. The ache sits inside practical behaviour: checking supplies, placing wristbands, pushing off. The wristbands must remain vacant. Keen must not look fearless; his brave face is a performance, and the audience should love him for trying.

beats.sourceScript: Keen loads and re-checks the boat while his Mum watches with pride she is trying not to let spill into tears.
exactDialogue: KEEN'S MUM: Keen… are you sure you’ve got everything?
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Keen wants the packing to certify him as ready. Keen's Mum wants one more check that is really one more moment with him.
beats.opposition: The boat rocks under each tidy placement, and Mum’s question carries more feeling than the words admit.
beats.subtext: Keen is not only checking supplies; he is checking whether he can convince Mum and himself. Mum is not asking about objects so much as asking whether he is safe enough to leave.
beats.beginningState: Keen is in active, forward-moving preparation; Mum stands back, proud but close to tears.
beats.pressure: The departure is imminent. If Mum says too much, she may make it harder; if Keen slows down, he may feel the size of leaving.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Keen over-organizes one item after another, then answers quickly to keep the moment from deepening.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is Keen’s line, “I’ve got this, Mum.” It lands as a brave badge and a small cover at the same time.
beats.consequence: Mum accepts the cover for now, but the audience sees the gap between his confident words and the care with which he keeps re-checking.
beats.reaction: Mum lets a tiny proud smile arrive before she has fully controlled the wetness behind it.
beats.closingState: Keen appears ready on the surface; Mum knows the goodbye has begun.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: Children feel the excitement of going; adults feel the parent measuring every ordinary object as a last chance to protect him.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Emotion engine: practical behaviour carrying separation. No gag; the packing is the mask.
beats.energyCurve: Busy, clipped, purposeful; then a small emotional catch under the line.
beats.memorableImage: Keen patting the same packed item one time too many while Mum watches as if that little pat might keep him safe.

interpretations.name: Keen’s proof-of-readiness beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Keen: packing is his audition for independence, and Mum’s question threatens to expose that the confidence is rehearsed.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Keen moves quickly, re-checks too precisely, and answers before his body has finished settling.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience smiles at his eagerness while sensing he is borrowing certainty.

interpretations.name: Mum’s delay beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Mum: every question is a loving stall, and the drama is whether she can avoid making him carry her fear.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Mum nearly steps in to adjust something, stops herself, and lets the question do the touching her paws cannot.
interpretations.audienceExperience: Adults feel the restraint; children read care through her checking.

interpretations.name: The boat’s threshold beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The boat is the emotional device: each object placed aboard makes leaving more real, while the dock remains the safe world.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Keen crosses between pier and boat in tiny practical transfers; Mum stays planted on the pier.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The geography tells the story before the words do.

beats.selectedDirectorialInterpretation: Keen’s proof-of-readiness beat, with Mum’s delay visible underneath.
beats.selectionReason: It best serves the episode premise: Keen begins by performing readiness. Mum’s ache must be felt, but the scene’s engine is Keen trying to make 'I’ve got this' true by saying it confidently enough.

beats.sourceScript: Mum admits the step is large; Keen looks out at the water, swallows, and answers with the line he has borrowed from her.
exactDialogue: KEEN'S MUM: I know… it’s just… this is a big step.
KEEN: Like you said… it’s part of growing up.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Mum wants to name the size of the moment without stopping him. Keen wants to use Mum’s own wisdom as a handrail so neither of them has to say they are afraid.
beats.opposition: The open water is now visible as distance, not scenery; Keen’s throat catches before his borrowed line can come out.
beats.subtext: Mum is asking permission to feel the bigness. Keen is answering with something she taught him because his own words are not steady yet.
beats.beginningState: The scene has slowed from packing into the awareness of the horizon.
beats.pressure: If Keen looks too long at the water, the brave performance may crack before he has even left.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Keen looks out, swallows, then chooses the line that sounds grown-up because it came from Mum.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is the swallow before the answer: his body tells the truth before his words put the mask back on.
beats.consequence: The line comforts Mum and exposes Keen’s vulnerability at once.
beats.reaction: Mum receives the echoed phrase with a soft hit of recognition: he has been listening, and he is still little enough to need her words.
beats.closingState: The goodbye becomes mutual courage rather than simple departure.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: A small breath-in: the child sees Keen being brave; the adult hears a child using a parent’s words to hold himself together.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Emotion engine: borrowed language as visible need. No gag.
beats.energyCurve: Stillness, swallow, careful line, quiet recognition.
beats.memorableImage: Keen facing the water with his answer caught halfway between his throat and the horizon.

interpretations.name: Borrowed wisdom beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: Keen’s line is a borrowed tool; the drama is whether it steadies him enough to continue.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: He looks outward first, then back only after he has secured the words.
interpretations.audienceExperience: We feel the tenderness of a child carrying a parent’s phrase into a hard moment.

interpretations.name: Mum’s permission beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: Mum tests whether she is allowed to admit this is hard; Keen grants permission by repeating her own lesson.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Mum softens when she hears herself returned to her, not as correction but as courage.
interpretations.audienceExperience: Adults feel seen in the letting-go; kids feel the seriousness without lecture.

interpretations.name: Water-as-opposition beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The horizon becomes the antagonist: the line exists because the water has made the step visibly large.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Keen’s body angles forward, but the swallow pins him for a breath.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The world makes the feeling legible.

beats.selectionReason: The episode is about borrowed confidence becoming real courage. This beat must show the borrowing cleanly before the storm takes it apart.

beats.sourceScript: Mum reveals the worn vacant wristbands and names their meaning; Keen stills as the breeze moves through the pier ropes.
exactDialogue: KEEN'S MUM: Keen… it’s time for you to have your father’s wristbands.
KEEN'S MUM: I still feel him… every day.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Mum wants to pass on memory without making it a burden. Keen wants to understand the object before he knows how to hold the feeling inside it.
beats.opposition: The wristbands are vacant, worn, and heavy with absence; the pier breeze moves because the bears cannot.
beats.subtext: Mum is saying: your father is gone, but not absent from us. Keen is hearing: this journey is no longer just mine.
beats.beginningState: Keen is still in departure mode, ready to move; Mum shifts the moment into ceremony.
beats.pressure: Once the wristbands are revealed, neither of them can pretend this is only packing and a boat ride.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Mum opens her keeping place and reveals the wristbands rather than continuing to protect them from the day.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is Keen’s stillness at the reveal: forward momentum stops because memory has entered the scene.
beats.consequence: The pier’s small motions become audible and visible around their silence; the wristbands claim the centre of the frame.
beats.reaction: Keen’s paws do not reach immediately. He needs the moment to arrive before he can accept it.
beats.closingState: The goodbye has become an inheritance handoff.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: A quiet intake: children understand the specialness of the object; adults feel the parent sharing grief as protection.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Emotion engine: object as held memory. No gag.
beats.energyCurve: Motion drops away into a reverent still point.
beats.memorableImage: The vacant wristbands held between Mum and Keen while the pier ropes shift in the breeze around them.

interpretations.name: Mum’s ceremony beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: Mum controls the reveal, and the drama is her choice to open her hands on something she has kept close.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Her handling is precise and slow, not decorative; each small movement is a decision to let go.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience feels the cost of generosity.

interpretations.name: Keen’s interruption beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Keen’s stopped momentum: the object interrupts his adventure fantasy with family history.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: He freezes before reaching, his usual forward lean suspended.
interpretations.audienceExperience: We feel the weight land on him in real time.

interpretations.name: The wristbands’ absence beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The vacant settings are the centre: the drama is not what shines, but what is missing and waiting.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Both characters become witnesses to the object rather than performers of the scene.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience understands the setup for later glow without being told.

beats.selectedDirectorialInterpretation: Mum’s ceremony beat with the wristbands’ absence held in the image.
beats.selectionReason: The emotional ownership of the reveal is Mum’s; she is giving away a connection to someone she still feels every day. The vacant state must be clear, but not colder than her love.

beats.sourceScript: Mum places the vacant wristbands into Keen's paws, asks for the promise, and he slips them on as she brushes his cheek.
exactDialogue: KEEN'S MUM: Promise me you’ll always wear them.
KEEN'S MUM: Wherever you go… You’ll never be alone.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Mum wants the wristbands to become a promise, not just an heirloom. Keen wants to accept them in a way that proves he can carry what they mean.
beats.opposition: His paws are small against the emotional size of the promise; putting them on makes the absence permanent and portable.
beats.subtext: Mum is asking him to carry family into fear. Keen is promising more than he fully understands, but he means it completely.
beats.beginningState: The wristbands are between them, not yet his.
beats.pressure: This is the last chance for Mum to place protection on him before he leaves the dock.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Mum transfers the wristbands into Keen’s paws; Keen chooses to put them on rather than simply hold them.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is the contact: the wristbands pass into Keen’s paws and the promise becomes physical.
beats.consequence: Once on him, the wristbands change the silhouette of the departure; he is leaving with family visibly carried.
beats.reaction: Mum’s cheek brush follows the promise because her voice has reached its limit; touch finishes the sentence.
beats.closingState: Keen is now cuffed with vacant wristbands and held by the promise, though the pier is about to release him.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: Children read the wristbands as special protection; adults feel the paradox of protecting a child by letting him leave.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Emotion engine: touch completing what words cannot. No gag.
beats.energyCurve: Tender concentration, promise, physical settling, soft release.
beats.memorableImage: Mum’s paw brushing Keen’s cheek just after the vacant wristbands settle onto him.

interpretations.name: Promise-as-action beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat is built around the promise becoming wearable; the line and the object fuse into one action.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Keen puts them on with care, then holds still for Mum’s touch instead of rushing onward.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience feels the promise land in the body.

interpretations.name: Mum’s last protection beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Mum: placing the wristbands is the last thing she can do before the world takes over.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Her touch lingers only long enough to bless, not enough to pull him back.
interpretations.audienceExperience: Adults feel the discipline of not clinging.

interpretations.name: Keen’s inheritance test beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Keen’s decision to accept weight; the drama is whether he treats the wristbands as treasure or responsibility.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: He begins eager, then slows when the promise is asked.
interpretations.audienceExperience: Children sense that special objects can ask something of you.

beats.selectionReason: This is the cleanest scene turn: words become object, object becomes vow, vow becomes the thing Keen will carry into the storm. It also keeps performance concrete and readable for young viewers.

beats.sourceScript: Keen absorbs the promise, smiles for real, and he and his Mum say the love they can say before the leaving begins.
exactDialogue: KEEN: I won’t be. I love you, Mum.
KEEN'S MUM: I love you… my brave boy.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Keen wants to reassure Mum truthfully now, not just perform readiness. Mum wants to name his bravery as love, not pressure.
beats.opposition: The words are simple, but saying them makes the separation real.
beats.subtext: Keen’s 'I won’t be' means he accepts being held by love even when physically alone. Mum’s 'brave boy' is pride threaded with fear.
beats.beginningState: The promise is newly on Keen; both are absorbing it.
beats.pressure: There is only a small space left before practical departure must interrupt feeling.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Keen lets a real smile arrive before speaking, choosing sincerity over the earlier quick cover.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is the real smile: for a moment he is not proving anything, just receiving the promise.
beats.consequence: The love exchange lands cleanly and warmly, giving the goodbye a secure centre.
beats.reaction: Mum answers with warmth that almost catches on the word 'brave,' but she does not make him carry the catch.
beats.closingState: They are emotionally connected enough for the physical leaving to begin.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: Warm ache: the child hears love; the parent hears the courage of sending love instead of fear.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Emotion engine: sincerity replacing performance. No gag.
beats.energyCurve: Quiet, open, warm, then poised to move.
beats.memorableImage: Keen’s first unguarded smile after the wristbands are on.

interpretations.name: Keen’s real-smile beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat turns on the difference between performed confidence and received love; Keen’s smile is the proof.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: His body settles before the line, no extra bounce to sell it.
interpretations.audienceExperience: We feel him become safer inside the goodbye.

interpretations.name: Mum’s naming beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Mum naming him 'my brave boy,' and the drama is whether that label comforts or burdens.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: She keeps the phrase soft so it lands as blessing, not expectation.
interpretations.audienceExperience: Adults hear the care in not overloading him.

interpretations.name: Mutual release beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat is a shared pact: they say just enough love to release each other into the next action.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Both let the words finish without rushing to fill the silence.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The scene breathes, then moves before sentiment pools.

beats.selectionReason: The episode needs one clear contrast before the comic push-off: Keen can be sincere. That gives emotional value to his later return to cover-up with 'Still got it!'

beats.sourceScript: Keen climbs into the boat, pushes off, wobbles, flails, catches himself, and covers with a proud little button.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Keen wants his first visible act of departure to look competent. Mum wants to let him recover without rescuing the moment for him.
beats.opposition: The boat answers his big confident push with an immediate bob that moves his balance out from under him.
beats.subtext: Keen’s cover says, please count that as success. Mum’s restraint says, I saw the wobble and I still believe in you.
beats.beginningState: After the tender goodbye, Keen returns to action mode to avoid lingering.
beats.pressure: Mum is watching, and this is his first chance to prove the brave-boy title fits.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Keen commits too much force into the push-off; the boat’s recoil travels up through him, tipping his balance until he grabs stability and chooses to cover instead of admit the scare.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is the boat’s bob stealing his triumphant launch.
beats.consequence: His proud departure becomes a barely saved wobble, with the boat now actually separating from the dock.
beats.reaction: Keen snaps into a proud button as if the wobble were planned. Mum’s laugh catches through a tear rather than correcting him.
beats.closingState: The boat is away; Keen’s false bravado is restored, but now lovingly exposed.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: A laugh with tenderness: children enjoy the wobble; adults recognize the cover-up as a child trying to leave well.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Hiding failure: the cover-up, not the wobble, is the joke.
beats.energyCurve: Tender stillness breaks into physical comedy, then lands on a proud little mask.
beats.memorableImage: Keen standing a fraction too proudly in a boat that has just proved it can boss him around.

interpretations.name: Keen’s cover-up gag
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Keen’s failed competence display; the punchline is his refusal to let the wobble count.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: He overcommits, recovers, then plants the line as if presenting evidence of mastery.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience laughs because they saw the truth he is decorating.

interpretations.name: Mum’s release-laugh beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The wobble exists to let Mum laugh through the tear, converting ache into permission to go.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: She does not lunge to help; her laugh is trust under strain.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience feels goodbye made survivable by a small joke.

interpretations.name: Boat-as-comic-partner beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The boat becomes the active opponent, undercutting Keen’s heroic launch with honest physics.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Keen’s confidence meets the boat’s bob; his recovery is a negotiation with the environment.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The world participates in humbling him without cruelty.

beats.selectionReason: It pays the episode’s false-bravado language and keeps the goodbye from becoming too sweet. The boat’s physics must cause the joke, but Keen’s character-specific cover is the laugh.

beats.sourceScript: Mum laughs through a tear, Squeaky splashes up beside the boat, and Keen startles into delighted curiosity.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Squeaky wants playful contact with the departing boat. Keen wants to turn surprise into discovery. Mum wants her last view of him to be alive with wonder, not only leaving.
beats.opposition: Squeaky’s sudden splash breaks Keen’s fragile balance and interrupts the emotional goodbye from an unexpected direction.
beats.subtext: The world is already meeting Keen. Mum can see he is being invited forward, not simply taken away.
beats.beginningState: Keen has just covered his wobble; Mum is laughing through emotion.
beats.pressure: The boat is drifting farther from the pier; this may be Mum’s final close look at him before distance takes over.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Squeaky’s splash throws water and surprise into the frame; Keen startles, then chooses curiosity over embarrassment.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is Keen’s startled 'Whoa!' flipping into 'Hey there!'
beats.consequence: The goodbye’s focus shifts from separation to first new friendship, and Keen’s body orients away from the pier for the first time with delight.
beats.reaction: Mum’s tearful laugh softens into relieved pride as she sees him meet the unknown rather than shrink from it.
beats.closingState: Keen is no longer only leaving Mum; he is beginning the adventure.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: Children light up at Squeaky’s entrance; adults feel the relief of seeing the child welcomed by the wider world.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Anticipation → reversal: after the wobbly proud exit, the next challenge is not danger but a playful splash that turns fear into curiosity.
beats.energyCurve: Release laugh, sudden splash, startle, delighted lift.
beats.memorableImage: Keen caught between dock and open water, dripping from Squeaky’s greeting and already leaning toward her.

interpretations.name: Squeaky-as-invitation beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: Squeaky’s arrival reframes the departure as welcome into a larger world.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Keen’s startle resolves into forward curiosity; Mum witnesses the shift.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The audience feels adventure arrive with friendliness.

interpretations.name: Keen’s curiosity-over-pride beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat tests whether Keen will protect his dignity after the wobble or engage the surprise.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: He begins embarrassed by being startled, then cannot resist greeting Squeaky.
interpretations.audienceExperience: The laugh comes from his quick conversion of alarm into enthusiasm.

interpretations.name: Mum’s last-image beat
interpretations.dramaticConstruction: The beat belongs to Mum receiving a better last image: her son not alone, already connecting.
interpretations.characterBehaviour: Her laugh through tears becomes relief when Squeaky appears beside him.
interpretations.audienceExperience: Adults get the ache-release; children get the splash.

beats.selectionReason: It supports the episode’s relationship map: Squeaky must begin as playful stranger and future rescue partner. The scene needs to pivot from home to world through relationship, not spectacle.

beats.sourceScript: Squeaky chatters, Keen nods as if he understands, and the boat glides farther from the dock as he looks ahead nervous and excited at once.
exactDialogue: KEEN: Nice to meet you too.
beats.objectiveByCharacter: Keen wants to belong in the adventure immediately, even to a language he does not understand. Squeaky wants playful companionship. Mum wants to hold the sight of him moving forward.
beats.opposition: The boat keeps gliding away from the dock, increasing the distance while Squeaky’s chatter gives Keen something new to focus on.
beats.subtext: Keen does not understand Squeaky, but he wants connection badly enough to act as if he does. His nerves and excitement now coexist openly.
beats.beginningState: Squeaky is beside the boat; Keen has turned toward her with curiosity.
beats.pressure: Each glide takes Keen farther from Mum and closer to the open water test he cannot yet imagine.
beats.actionDiscoveryOrChoice: Squeaky chatters; Keen nods with too much confidence, choosing friendly participation over admitting confusion.
beats.reversalReleaseOrRecognition: The turn is Keen answering as if fluent: “Nice to meet you too.”
beats.consequence: The audience understands that the bond is real even if the translation is nonsense, and the boat’s distance from the dock quietly increases.
beats.reaction: Squeaky stays engaged; Keen’s face holds both thrill and a swallowed wobble as he looks ahead. Mum remains behind, smaller in relation to the widening water, but connected by the wristbands on him.
beats.closingState: Keen is launched into the unknown with a new companion nearby, a promise on his wrists, and nerves still visible under the excitement.
beats.intendedAudienceResponse: A gentle laugh at Keen’s pretend fluency, followed by a small ache as the dock recedes.
beats.comedyOrEmotionEngine: Misunderstanding: Keen nods along to Squeaky’s chatter as if fluent, and the confidence of the response is the joke.
beats.energyCurve: Playful chatter and nodding ease into a widening, nervous-excited glide.
beats.memorableImage: Keen nodding solemnly to Squeaky’s chatter while the dock slips farther behind him.

showrunnerJudgement: Passes. The scene works as one audience experience: the practical packing earns the emotional handoff, the vacant wristbands stay rightly restrained, and the wobble/Squeaky arrival releases the ache before it becomes syrup. Keen’s want/need gap is readable with the sound off: he performs readiness while his body keeps confessing the size of leaving. Mum’s restraint is the adult door, Keen’s over-brave recovery is the child door, and the wristbands give the scene its memorable image. Camera, body, and voice are aligned around physical causality — item shifts, boat bobs, paws hesitate, weight transfers — so the emotion is played through action rather than explained. The final glide keeps the cost visible by holding Mum smaller behind him, while Squeaky turns departure into beginning. This is Crystal Bears: warm, funny, specific, and carrying the ache forward rather than resolving it away.

internalRevisions.issue: The composition says Keen and Squeaky occupy the small moving boat, which contradicts the established staging of Squeaky splashing and travelling beside the boat at waterline. Keep Squeaky alongside in the water, not in the boat, so the image remains: Keen leaving home in the boat, Squeaky as the new world keeping pace, Mum receding behind, wristbands visibly carried.
